title: Voice-enabled RAG overview
text: A voice-enabled retrieval-augmented generation system accepts spoken input, converts speech to text, retrieves grounded context, and produces an answer based on that context. The pipeline should work end to end instead of handling speech and retrieval as disconnected steps.

title: Chunking strategy
text: Strong retrieval quality depends on more than one naive chunking approach. A practical system can mix semantic chunking, overlapping fixed-size chunks, and metadata-aware splitting so that different query styles still find relevant evidence.

title: Latency analytics
text: Latency reporting should include p50, p70, and p100 measured over multiple realistic test queries. A single best-case timing is not enough to describe performance.

title: Harness and guardrails
text: A proper harness includes structured inputs and outputs, retries or controlled failure paths, and orchestration across pipeline stages. Guardrails should detect unsafe requests, off-topic questions, and answers that are not grounded in retrieved evidence.

title: Refusal behavior
text: The system should refuse to answer when the query is unsafe, when the request is off-topic for the indexed corpus, or when retrieval does not produce grounded evidence strong enough to support a reliable answer.
